## What is wrong (one paragraph)
`.githooks/pre-push:268` is a load-bearing comment: it is the rationale for sourcing `slot-target.sh` before the preflight so the stack-dependent legs probe THIS slot. It names those legs as **(3, 4, 7)**; measured 2026-09-09 they are **3, 4, 8** (leg 7 is the standalone-lock advisories, not stack-dependent; leg 8, served-spec consistency, is) — a leg was inserted and the comment did not move. The ticket's better fix, in the spirit of KS-1046 (#925, which made the verdict PRINT the skipped legs): drop the enumeration and point at the verdict line, which cannot drift. **This task: line 268 becomes a pointer to the verdict, plus one new shell suite proving the stale enumeration is gone, the pointer is present, and the comment's anchor and the hook's syntax are untouched.** NOT in this task: :269–:274 (the rest of the comment), any code.

Do not add, drop, re-indent or reword a line; do not add a trailing comment; do not mark a context line as `+`.  # Safe on macOS bash 3.2: the script uses no bash-4 constructs (no mapfile/readarray,

-# KS-691: source slot-target.sh first so the stack-dependent legs (3, 4, 7) probe

Every value a cell reads is assigned above the first cell. **Your diff for this file is a NEW-FILE diff: `--- /dev/null`, `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_stack_legs_comment.test.sh`, ONE hunk header `@@ -0,0 +1,74 @@`, then EVERY line with a leading `+` (a blank line is a lone `+`) - no context lines, no `-` lines: you are not diffing the reference.**

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for .githooks/pre-push line :268 comment - stale leg enumeration gone, pointer present (KS-1047)
# =============================================================================
# The defect at tip `48e65c435`: line 268 enumerates legs "(3, 4, 7)" which is
# wrong (measured 2026-09-09 they are 3, 4, 8). The fix drops the enumeration
# and points at the verdict line instead. These four cells prove that.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_stack_legs_comment.test.sh
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail
TOTAL_CELLS=4

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
SUBJ="${PRE_PUSH_HOOK-$REPO_ROOT/.githooks/pre-push}"
[ -f "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: pre-push hook not found at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -r "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: PRE_PUSH_HOOK is not readable at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
printf 'SUBJECT %s\n        sha256 %s\n\n' "$SUBJ" "$(shasum -a 256 "$SUBJ" | cut -d" " -f1)"

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 1 - KS-1047 RED. THE STALE ENUMERATION IS GONE.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
stale_hits="$(grep -c '(3, 4, 7)' "$SUBJ" || true)"
if [ "$stale_hits" = 0 ]; then
  ok "the stale leg enumeration (3, 4, 7) is gone from pre-push"
else
  bad "the stale leg enumeration (3, 4, 7) is gone from pre-push" \
      "count=$stale_hits (expected 0)"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 2 - KS-1047 RED. THE COMMENT POINTS AT THE VERDICT LINE (KS-1046), NOT LEGS.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ptr_hits="$(grep -c 'KS-1046' "$SUBJ" || true)"
if [ "$ptr_hits" = 1 ]; then
  ok "the comment points at the verdict line (KS-1046) instead of enumerating legs"
else
  bad "the comment points at the verdict line (KS-1046) instead of enumerating legs" \
      "count=$ptr_hits (expected 1)"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 3 - CONTROL. THE KS-691 RATIONALE COMMENT IS STILL THERE.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
anchor_hits="$(grep -c 'KS-691: source slot-target.sh first so the stack-dependent legs' "$SUBJ" || true)"
if [ "$anchor_hits" = 1 ]; then
  ok "the KS-691 rationale comment anchor is still present in pre-push"
else
  bad "the KS-691 rationale comment anchor is still present in pre-push" \
      "count=$anchor_hits (expected 1)"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 4 - CONTROL. PRE-PUSH PARSes (bash -n).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if bash -n "$SUBJ" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ok "pre-push parses (bash -n)"
else
  bad "pre-push parses (bash -n)" "$(bash -n "$SUBJ" 2>&1 | head -5 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed (of %d cells)\n' "$pass" "$fail" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
# A cell that never ran is not a pass: the ratio must add up.
if [ "$((pass + fail))" -ne "$TOTAL_CELLS" ]; then
  printf '  INCOMPLETE - %d of %d cells ran\n' "$((pass + fail))" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
  exit 1
fi
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
```

#!/bin/sh
# .githooks/pre-push (KS-380) — run the preflight gate before a push leaves the machine.
#
# Fires only when the push includes changes under Blockchain/Dev (platform code);
# skips instantly for vault-only / docs-only / systemTest-only pushes so it stays
# out of the way. The preflight itself skips any leg whose deps aren't up (Docker
# down → lockfile leg advisory; stack down → auth-conformance leg skipped), so a
# normal push is never blocked by infrastructure being off — CI is the hard gate.
#
# Enable once per clone:
#   git config core.hooksPath .githooks && chmod +x .githooks/pre-push
# Bypass a single push (use sparingly): git push --no-verify

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# KS-856 — REFUSE A NON-FAST-FORWARD PUSH TO A BRANCH THAT EXISTS AT ORIGIN.
#
# The standing rule is: no force push; a rebase becomes a NEW branch. Nothing
# enforced it. Twice in one session an agent began a push that would have
# rewritten or moved a branch another process depended on, and both times the
# only thing that stopped it was noticing at human speed before the hook
# finished. A rule that survives on attention is not a control.
#
# THIS RUNS FIRST, BEFORE THE Blockchain/Dev EARLY RETURN BELOW. If it ran
# after, a force push carrying only docs would take the `[ -z "$changed" ]
# && exit 0` path and skip the check entirely — the gate would be conditional
# on what the push happened to touch, which is not the property being held.
#
# git feeds this hook one line per ref on stdin:
#     <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>
# An all-zero REMOTE sha means the branch does not exist at origin — a new
# branch, which is the sanctioned path and always passes. An all-zero LOCAL sha
# is a deletion, which rewrites no history.
#
# Deliberate force is still possible, but it cannot happen by reflex:
#     ALLOW_FORCE=1 git push ...
#
# NOT closed by this: a legal FAST-FORWARD onto a head that is under a running
# gate (the other near-miss). That push is a fast-forward and the hook cannot
# know what is gated. Named here so this is not read as covering both.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
force_refused=0
while read -r _local_ref local_sha _remote_ref remote_sha; do
    [ -z "$local_sha" ] && continue
    [ "$local_sha" = "$ZERO" ] && continue      # deleting a branch rewrites nothing
    [ "$remote_sha" = "$ZERO" ] && continue     # brand-new branch at origin
    if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$remote_sha" "$local_sha" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "[pre-push] REFUSED — non-fast-forward push to a branch that exists at origin." >&2
        echo "           ref:    ${_remote_ref}" >&2
        echo "           origin: ${remote_sha}" >&2
        echo "           local:  ${local_sha}" >&2
        echo "           The rule is: NO FORCE PUSH — a rebase becomes a NEW branch." >&2
        echo "           Landing this would rewrite history another process may depend on:" >&2
        echo "           an open PR's head, or a gate running against the SHA you are replacing." >&2
        echo "           Deliberate case, stated explicitly:  ALLOW_FORCE=1 git push ..." >&2
        force_refused=1
    fi
done
if [ "$force_refused" -eq 1 ]; then
    if [ "${ALLOW_FORCE:-0}" = "1" ]; then
        echo "[pre-push] ALLOW_FORCE=1 — proceeding with a non-fast-forward push, deliberately." >&2
    else
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# Are any Blockchain/Dev files in the commits about to be pushed?
#
# KS-989: the FULL changed list is captured once, and both filters read from it —
# the Blockchain/Dev one on the next line (which decides the preflight) and the
# systemTest/* one further down (which decides the formatting gate). This line
# used to grep at the point of capture and throw the rest away, which is exactly
# why a systemTest-only push was priced as costless: there was no list left to
# ask a second question of.
all_changed=$(git diff --name-only "@{upstream}" HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)
changed=$(printf '%s\n' "$all_changed" | grep '^Blockchain/Dev/' || true)
st_all=0   # KS-989: 1 = check every systemTest package, for the two cases below

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# KS-854 — A BASE THAT CANNOT BE COMPUTED IS NOT AN EMPTY DIFF.
#
# New branch with no upstream yet → diff against the merge-base with develop.
# This used to be a bare `git merge-base develop HEAD`, and on a FRESH CLONE
# `develop` does not resolve: `git clone` creates only the default branch
# locally, so develop exists solely as `refs/remotes/origin/develop`. The
# command failed into a `$(…)` with stderr discarded, `base` was empty,
# `changed` stayed empty, and the `[ -z "$changed" ] && exit 0` below returned
# success BEFORE leg 1 — no preflight, and no line saying so.
#
# Measured (KS-854 regression suite, and by the #840 gate by accident): a clone
# whose only local branch is `main`, on a branch with no upstream, carrying a
# real Blockchain/Dev change, pushed rc 0 in seconds with NO `[pre-push]` output
# whatsoever. Anyone who clones fresh and branches off `origin/develop` got no
# gate at all and no signal that they had none.
#
# Two changes, and the second is the load-bearing one:
#   1. resolve the base against the first ref that actually EXISTS, so the
#      normal fresh-clone case (origin/develop present) simply works; and
#   2. when NO base can be computed, RUN the preflight and say why. An empty
#      result must never be read as a pass — that is the same shape as the
#      CVE scan that reported clean having examined nothing (KS-676), and as
#      leg 9 passing a planted violation (KS-853). Failing safe here costs a
#      preflight run in a rare configuration; failing open costs the gate.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# KS-882 — A BASE THAT CONTAINS HEAD IS NOT A CLEAN TREE EITHER.
#
# The loop above used to stop at the FIRST ref that produced a base, and diff
# against that one alone. Local `develop` is tried first, so a local `develop`
# that already CONTAINS the branch tip made `git merge-base develop HEAD`
# return HEAD, `git diff HEAD HEAD` return nothing, and the
# `[ -z "$changed" ] && exit 0` below return success — push rc 0, zero
# `[pre-push]` lines, preflight never invoked, while `origin/develop` still
# held the old content. A real Blockchain/Dev change went up ungated and
# nothing said so. Same shape as KS-854 above, one ref further along: AN EMPTY
# RESULT READ AS A PASS.
#
# Two properties, and the second is the one the obvious fix misses:
#   1. Do not stop at the first base — ask EVERY resolvable ref and run the
#      gate if ANY of them shows a Blockchain/Dev change. Reordering the list
#      to put `origin/develop` first would close the reported instance and
#      leave the shape: whichever ref is consulted first can contain HEAD.
#   2. When EVERY resolvable base is HEAD itself, the empty diff carries no
#      information at all — there is no ref that can tell us what is new. That
#      is the KS-854 condition wearing a different hat, so it takes the same
#      answer: announce it and RUN, rather than skip in silence.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ -z "$changed" ] && ! git rev-parse '@{upstream}' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    base=''
    _informative=0
    _head=$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # KS-991 — A STALE LOCAL `develop` CAN ONLY INFLATE THE DIFF, SO SKIP IT.
    #
    # This is NOT a reorder, and the distinction is the whole justification.
    # KS-882's author considered putting `origin/develop` first and rejected it,
    # because whichever ref is consulted FIRST can contain HEAD. That reasoning
    # stands and is untouched: the union rule below still asks every remaining
    # ref and still runs unconditionally when none is informative.
    #
    # What is skipped here is only a ref that ANOTHER resolvable ref PROVABLY
    # supersedes — local `develop` when it is a strict ancestor of
    # `origin/develop`. The two failure directions are opposites:
    #
    #   KS-882  a ref CONTAINING the tip  -> empty diff    -> HIDES a change
    #   KS-991  a ref BEHIND the remote   -> inflated diff -> INVENTS a change
    #
    # A stale base sits at or behind the better base, so its diff is a SUPERSET:
    # it reports files that are on the trunk but not in this branch, and it
    # cannot conceal anything. Skipping it therefore costs no safety.
    #
    # Measured 2026-09-08: three pushes in ONE session ran the full 13-leg
    # Blockchain/Dev preflight on branches touching no Blockchain/Dev file —
    # ff5218867 vs 400517aaf, 400517aaf vs 4f337be83, 4f337be83 vs 512480ef1.
    # Every gap was opened by a merge the same seat had just performed, so the
    # trigger is "you did the right thing". One run then failed leg 1 with
    # DEPS MISSING — an environment condition presented as a gate result, and
    # indistinguishable from a real red without reading 13 legs of output.
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    _refs='develop origin/develop refs/remotes/origin/develop'
    if git rev-parse --verify --quiet develop >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
       git rev-parse --verify --quiet origin/develop >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
       [ "$(git rev-parse develop)" != "$(git rev-parse origin/develop)" ] &&
       git merge-base --is-ancestor develop origin/develop 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "[pre-push] KS-991: local 'develop' is BEHIND origin/develop — ignoring the" >&2
        echo "[pre-push]   stale ref for base selection. (git fetch origin develop:develop" >&2
        echo "[pre-push]   to refresh it.) origin/develop is still consulted below." >&2
        _refs='origin/develop refs/remotes/origin/develop'
    fi
    for _ref in $_refs; do
        git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$_ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue
        _b=$(git merge-base "$_ref" HEAD 2>/dev/null) || _b=''
        [ -n "$_b" ] || continue
        base="$_b"
        # A base equal to HEAD means this ref already contains the tip: it can
        # only ever produce an empty diff, so it is not evidence of anything.
        [ "$_b" = "$_head" ] && continue
        _informative=1
        _files=$(git diff --name-only "$_b" HEAD || true)
        # KS-989: keep the union of every ref consulted, for the systemTest gate.
        # The Blockchain/Dev decision on the next lines is byte-for-byte what it
        # was — same grep, same value, same break — so the KS-854 and KS-882
        # properties above are untouched. This only retains a list that used to
        # be discarded inside the pipe.
        all_changed=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$all_changed" "$_files")
        _c=$(printf '%s\n' "$_files" | grep '^Blockchain/Dev/' || true)
        if [ -n "$_c" ]; then
            changed="$_c"
            break
        fi
    done
    if [ -n "$base" ] && [ "$_informative" -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "[pre-push] KS-882: every ref that resolves already CONTAINS this commit," >&2
        echo "[pre-push]   so the diff against it is empty for that reason and not because" >&2
        echo "[pre-push]   the tree is clean. Running the preflight UNCONDITIONALLY." >&2
        echo "[pre-push]   (git fetch origin develop to give the gate a real base.)" >&2
        changed='KS-882: every base contains HEAD — running unconditionally'
        st_all=1   # KS-989: no usable changed set, so check EVERY systemTest package
    fi
    if [ -z "$base" ]; then
        echo "[pre-push] KS-854: no base to diff against — 'develop' does not resolve," >&2
        echo "[pre-push]   'origin/develop' does not resolve, and this branch has no upstream." >&2
        echo "[pre-push]   Running the preflight UNCONDITIONALLY: an uncomputable base is not" >&2
        echo "[pre-push]   the same as a clean one. (git fetch origin develop to silence this.)" >&2
        changed='KS-854: base unresolved — running unconditionally'
        st_all=1   # KS-989: no usable changed set, so check EVERY systemTest package
    fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# KS-989 — THE systemTest/* FORMATTING GATE.
#
# THIS RUNS BEFORE THE Blockchain/Dev EARLY RETURN BELOW, and that placement is
# the whole fix. A systemTest-only push takes `[ -z "$changed" ] && exit 0` and
# would never reach a gate placed after it — which is precisely the hole: six
# instances in nine days, three paid for by someone other than the author.
#
# It is CHEAP by construction (`format:check`, 0-2s per touched package, and
# nothing at all when the push touches no gated package), so the header's
# promise that this hook "stays out of the way" still holds. It is deliberately
# NOT `npm run quality` — see KS-990 and the script's own header: `quality`
# cannot pass in two of these packages today, and a gate that can never pass
# gets bypassed.
#
# The same KS-854/KS-882 rule applies to it as to the preflight: when no
# informative base could be computed, `st_all=1` checks EVERY package rather
# than reading an empty changed set as a clean tree.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)
_fmt_gate="$_toplevel/systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh"
if [ ! -f "$_fmt_gate" ]; then
    # The hook and the script land in the same commit, so this is not reachable
    # by branching. It IS reachable by deleting one of them, and a missing gate
    # that stays quiet is the failure this hook exists to stop.
    echo "[pre-push] REFUSED — the KS-989 formatting gate is missing at:" >&2
    echo "           $_fmt_gate" >&2
    echo "           A gate that cannot be found must not be read as a gate that passed." >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [ "$st_all" -eq 1 ]; then
    bash "$_fmt_gate" --all || {
        echo "[pre-push] systemTest formatting gate FAILED — fix the files named above." >&2
        echo "           (bypass, sparingly: git push --no-verify)" >&2
        exit 1
    }
else
    printf '%s\n' "$all_changed" | bash "$_fmt_gate" || {
        echo "[pre-push] systemTest formatting gate FAILED — fix the files named above." >&2
        echo "           (bypass, sparingly: git push --no-verify)" >&2
        exit 1
    }
fi

[ -z "$changed" ] && exit 0

echo "[pre-push] Blockchain/Dev changes detected → running preflight gate (bypass: --no-verify)"
# Invoke with `bash`, NOT `sh`. preflight.sh is `#!/usr/bin/env bash` and opens with
# `set -uo pipefail`, which is a bash builtin option: on Linux /bin/sh is dash, which
# rejects it with "Illegal option -o pipefail" and aborts the gate before leg 1 — so
# the preflight could never run on the Ubuntu VM, and every push there either failed
# or got --no-verify'd. Invisible on macOS, where /bin/sh is bash-in-POSIX-mode and
# accepts pipefail. Same portability class as KS-600 (`mktemp -t`).
# Naming the interpreter (rather than the bare path) is deliberate: preflight.sh is
# committed mode 100644, so a direct exec fails with "permission denied" — the
# KS-487 session note above. `bash <file>` needs no exec bit.
# Safe on macOS bash 3.2: the script uses no bash-4 constructs (no mapfile/readarray,
# no associative arrays, no ${x^^}).
# KS-691: source slot-target.sh first so the stack-dependent legs (3, 4, 7) probe
# THIS slot's gateway. preflight.sh defaults GATEWAY to localhost:6882 (slot 1),
# so from any other slot those legs either silently SKIP (slot 1 down) — the push
# passes having probed nothing — or probe SLOT 1 and report success for a stack
# you were not testing (slot 1 up). The second is the worse failure: it is a green
# gate describing the wrong system. slot-target.sh also unsets COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME,
# which must not leak into anything the preflight runs (KS-666).
( bash -c '
    cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" || exit 1
    . systemTest/slot-target.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    cd Blockchain/Dev && bash scripts/preflight/preflight.sh
  ' ) || {
    echo "[pre-push] preflight failed — fix the above, or bypass with: git push --no-verify" >&2
    exit 1
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docker-build.sh — an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE
# (KS-877)
# =============================================================================
# The defect: with an empty SERVICES_TABLE, `docker-build.sh all` died at the
# banner's `${BUILD_LIST[*]}` with `BUILD_LIST[*]: unbound variable` under
# bash 3.2 + `set -u` — three lines after the `[ -n ]` guard added for exactly
# this class. That guard works (BUILD_LIST is left genuinely empty); the display
# expansion after it does not. And `${BUILD_LIST[*]:-}` alone only moves the
# death 55 lines down to the parallel loop's `"${BUILD_LIST[@]}"` — measured —
# so the shape that holds is a guard on `${#BUILD_LIST[@]}` that names the
# table and exits before either.
#
# docker is NEVER run: a stub on a private PATH records every call and exits 0,
# so the control cells can prove the working path still builds without a
# daemon. The empty table is produced by a fixture COPY of the subject whose
# heredoc body is stripped — the table is a literal inside the script, so
# there is no other way to reach the path — and the copy's row count is
# asserted 29 -> 0 before the cell is scored.
#
# Round 2 (KS-877, the tier-2 gate's F1): CELL 3 was RED on the repository's CI
# (ubuntu, bash 5.x) while green on macOS — `docker-build.sh`'s `((RUNNING++))`
# exits 1 when RUNNING is 0, and bash >= 4.1 `set -e` (COMPAT item 45) kills the
# script on it; bash 3.2 does not. CELL 4 pins the construct's ABSENCE statically
# (this box has no bash >= 4.1; CI's CELL 3 is the runtime instrument) and CELL 5
# proves the fix does not swallow a genuine build failure. The summary line
# carries the cell count (`(of N cells)`) and the run FAILS if fewer cells ran.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/docker_build_empty_table.test.sh
#        DOCKER_BUILD_SH=/path/to/other/docker-build.sh bash …   (red-proof)
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail
TOTAL_CELLS=5

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
# Same subject discipline as orchestrate_jobs.test.sh (KS-923 F2 / KS-941).
if [ "${DOCKER_BUILD_SH+set}" = set ] && [ -z "$DOCKER_BUILD_SH" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: DOCKER_BUILD_SH is set but EMPTY — refusing to silently grade the shipped script." >&2
  exit 2
fi
SUBJ="${DOCKER_BUILD_SH-$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docker-build.sh}"
[ -f "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: docker-build.sh not found at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -r "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: DOCKER_BUILD_SH is not readable at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
printf 'SUBJECT %s\n        sha256 %s\n\n' "$SUBJ" "$(shasum -a 256 "$SUBJ" | cut -d" " -f1)"

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks877.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# Data rows of the SERVICES_TABLE heredoc in a script: tab-separated, not a
# comment. The same predicate service_names() applies.
table_rows() {
  sed -n "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/p" "$1" \
    | awk -F'\t' 'NF==2 && $1 !~ /^[[:space:]]*#/' | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

# Build a fixture project root around a copy of the script under test.
#   $1 = dir   $2 = table: intact | emptied
# The copy lives at <root>/scripts/docker-build.sh so the script's own
# `PROJECT_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/.."` resolves to the fixture root.
build_fixture() {
  local root="$1" table="$2"
  rm -rf "$root"; mkdir -p "$root/scripts" "$root/bin" "$root/services/auth"
  printf 'FROM scratch\n' > "$root/services/auth/Dockerfile"
  if [ "$table" = emptied ]; then
    # Strip every line between the heredoc's opening and closing markers.
    sed "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/{//!d;}" "$SUBJ" > "$root/scripts/docker-build.sh"
  else
    cp "$SUBJ" "$root/scripts/docker-build.sh"
  fi
  # docker stub: records every call, succeeds.
  { printf '#!/bin/bash\n'; printf 'echo "docker $*" >> "%s/docker_calls.txt"\nexit 0\n' "$root"; } > "$root/bin/docker"
  chmod +x "$root/bin/docker"
}

# Run the copy with ONLY the stub dir in front of the system dirs. Prints rc.
run_build() {
  local root="$1"; shift
  ( export PATH="$root/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"; cd "$root" && bash scripts/docker-build.sh "$@" ) >"$root/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}
build_calls() { if [ -f "$1/docker_calls.txt" ]; then grep -c '^docker build' "$1/docker_calls.txt" || true; else echo 0; fi; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 1 — KS-877. THE REGRESSION. An EMPTY table must be refused by name —
# "no services matched", naming SERVICES_TABLE — with NO `unbound variable`
# and no build attempted. Asserted on rc = 1 AND the ABSENCE of the
# unbound-variable death AND the PRESENCE of the message naming SERVICES_TABLE
# AND 0 builds. rc alone cannot discriminate base from head (both exit 1),
# which is why the other three clauses exist; it is asserted so that a guard
# that prints the message and then exits 0 still reds (the gate's Tk). The row
# count is a precondition: a copy that still has rows would pass the pre-fix
# script and say nothing.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/empty" emptied
rows_subj="$(table_rows "$SUBJ")"; rows_copy="$(table_rows "$WORK/empty/scripts/docker-build.sh")"
if [ "$rows_subj" -lt 1 ] || [ "$rows_copy" -ne 0 ]; then
  bad "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE is refused by name with no 'unbound variable'" \
      "precondition broken: subject rows=$rows_subj (expected >=1), emptied copy rows=$rows_copy (expected 0) — the cell cannot discriminate"
else
  rc_empty="$(run_build "$WORK/empty" all)"
  if [ "$rc_empty" = 1 ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" \
     && grep -q 'no services matched' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && grep -q 'SERVICES_TABLE' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" \
     && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/empty")" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE ($rows_subj rows -> $rows_copy) is refused by name — 'no services matched', naming SERVICES_TABLE — with no 'unbound variable', 0 builds, rc=$rc_empty"
  else
    bad "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE is refused by name with no 'unbound variable'" \
        "rc=$rc_empty, unbound variable present=$(grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo YES || echo no), message present=$(grep -q 'no services matched' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo yes || echo NO), table named=$(grep -q 'SERVICES_TABLE' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo yes || echo NO), builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/empty"), last lines: $(tail -2 "$WORK/empty/out.txt" | sed 's|.*/scripts/||' | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 2 — CONTROL (the working path, one service). The intact table with
# `auth` must still print `Services:  auth`, build it once via the stub, report
# BUILD OK and exit 0. Without this, CELL 1 could pass by a guard that refuses
# every list.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/one" intact
rc_one="$(run_build "$WORK/one" auth)"
if [ "$rc_one" = 0 ] && grep -q '^  Services:  auth$' "$WORK/one/out.txt" && grep -q '\[auth\] BUILD OK' "$WORK/one/out.txt" \
   && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/one")" -eq 1 ] && grep -q -- '-f services/auth/Dockerfile' "$WORK/one/docker_calls.txt"; then
  ok "CONTROL — the intact table with 'auth' prints 'Services:  auth', builds it once (-f services/auth/Dockerfile), BUILD OK, rc 0"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the intact table with 'auth' still builds it once and exits 0" \
      "rc=$rc_one, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/one"), output: $(grep -v '^=*$' "$WORK/one/out.txt" | tail -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 3 — CONTROL (the working path, every service, the parallel loop). The
# intact table with `all` must build every row via the stub and exit 0 — the
# path whose re-index guard (`${#PIDS[@]}`) the file's own comment documents,
# exercised under bash 3.2 with instant builds so the loop's empty-array case
# is actually reached.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/all" intact
rc_all="$(run_build "$WORK/all" all)"
if [ "$rc_all" = 0 ] && grep -q "SUCCEEDED ($rows_subj):" "$WORK/all/out.txt" && grep -q 'All builds succeeded' "$WORK/all/out.txt" \
   && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/all")" -eq "$rows_subj" ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/all/out.txt"; then
  ok "CONTROL — the intact table with 'all' builds every row ($rows_subj stub builds), SUCCEEDED ($rows_subj), rc 0, no unbound variable"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the intact table with 'all' builds every row and exits 0" \
      "rc=$rc_all, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/all") of $rows_subj, output: $(grep -i 'unbound\|SUCCEEDED\|FAILED' "$WORK/all/out.txt" | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 4 — KS-877 round 2 (the gate's F1). The subject has NO bare
# arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement (`((X++))` / `((X--))` on a line
# of its own). Such a command exits 1 when its expression evaluates to 0 — a
# post-increment yields the OLD value, so `((RUNNING++))` at RUNNING=0 "fails"
# — and bash >= 4.1 `set -e` exits on it (bash COMPAT item 45: "Bash-4.1 …
# exits when any command fails, not just a simple command or pipeline").
# bash 3.2 (macOS) does not, which is why CELL 3 was green here and RED on CI's
# ubuntu (run 34743050388: `rc=1, builds=0 of 29` — the script died after
# backgrounding ONE build). This is a STATIC pin, honest about being one: the
# runtime pin is CELL 3 on a bash >= 4.1, i.e. CI. The positive control inside
# the cell proves the grep can fire (a here-string holding `((X++))` -> 1).
# `[[:space:]]`, not `\s`: BSD grep.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARITH_RE='^[[:space:]]*\(\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*(\+\+|--)\)\)[[:space:]]*$'
arith_control="$(printf '  ((X++))\n' | grep -cE "$ARITH_RE" || true)"
arith_hits="$(grep -nE "$ARITH_RE" "$SUBJ" || true)"
arith_count="$(printf '%s' "$arith_hits" | grep -c . || true)"
if [ "$arith_control" != 1 ]; then
  bad "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement" \
      "instrument cannot fire: the positive control read $arith_control (expected 1) — the cell is not scoring the subject"
elif [ "$arith_count" -eq 0 ]; then
  ok "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement — ((X++)) exits 1 at 0 and bash >= 4.1 set -e dies on it (control fires: $arith_control)"
else
  bad "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement" \
      "count=$arith_count (control=$arith_control): $(printf '%s' "$arith_hits" | sed 's/^\([0-9]*\):[[:space:]]*/:\1 /' | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 5 — KS-877 round 2, the MASK CONTROL. A run where ONE build genuinely
# fails must still land in `FAILED (1)` with rc 1 and the summary printed —
# the counter fix must not swallow a real failure. A second stub records the
# call, then exits 1 when its args name services/auth/Dockerfile (asserted
# unique among the table's rows). On bash 3.2 this reads the SAME before and
# after the fix — that IS the control: the fix changes nothing 3.2 can see
# except the arithmetic status; on CI (bash 5.x) it exercises the fixed loop
# under a genuine failure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/onefail" intact
{ printf '#!/bin/bash\n'; printf 'echo "docker $*" >> "%s/docker_calls.txt"\ncase "$*" in *services/auth/Dockerfile*) exit 1;; esac\nexit 0\n' "$WORK/onefail"; } > "$WORK/onefail/bin/docker"
chmod +x "$WORK/onefail/bin/docker"
auth_rows="$(sed -n "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/p" "$WORK/onefail/scripts/docker-build.sh" \
  | awk -F'\t' 'NF==2 && $1 !~ /^[[:space:]]*#/ && $2 == "services/auth/Dockerfile"' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
if [ "$auth_rows" -ne 1 ]; then
  bad "MASK CONTROL — one genuinely failing build still lands in FAILED (1), rc 1" \
      "precondition broken: $auth_rows table rows resolve to services/auth/Dockerfile (expected exactly 1) — the failing stub cannot be aimed"
else
  rc_onefail="$(run_build "$WORK/onefail" all)"
  if [ "$rc_onefail" = 1 ] && grep -q "SUCCEEDED ($((rows_subj - 1))):" "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" && grep -q 'FAILED (1):' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" \
     && grep -q '^    auth$' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" && ! grep -q 'All builds succeeded' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" \
     && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/onefail")" -eq "$rows_subj" ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt"; then
    ok "MASK CONTROL — with the auth stub exiting 1, 'all' still runs every row ($rows_subj stub builds), SUCCEEDED ($((rows_subj - 1))), FAILED (1): auth, rc 1"
  else
    bad "MASK CONTROL — one genuinely failing build still lands in FAILED (1), rc 1" \
        "rc=$rc_onefail, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/onefail") of $rows_subj, output: $(grep -i 'unbound\|SUCCEEDED\|FAILED\|All builds' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" | head -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed (of %d cells)\n' "$pass" "$fail" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
# A cell that never ran is not a pass (KS-877 round 2): the ratio must add up.
if [ "$((pass + fail))" -ne "$TOTAL_CELLS" ]; then
  printf '  INCOMPLETE — %d of %d cells ran\n' "$((pass + fail))" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
  exit 1
fi
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
